title: The Library: The Indifference of Description
description: A nonfiction book that follows the algorithmic information theory of the 1960s to a cold conclusion and a chosen response. Generating everything is trivial: every possible book, every computable description, is the output of a short program. What is hard is picking anything out of it. Built on theorems (Bayes' theorem, Kraft's inequality, Solomonoff's dominance theorem), one universal construction (the universal prior), and a single labeled postulate (no carving of the totality is privileged), the book traces the consequences for continuation, mortality, love, memory, and the self, and arrives at the indifference of description and the warmth we choose to provide each other inside it. Volume III of the Indifference suite, after Worldlines (geometry) and Multitudes (measure).
